t.3.67.1: O long-armed Rāma of great strength and valour, formerly my form was inconceivable and renowned throughout the three worlds, like the body of Soma, of Śakra, and of Sūrya.
t.3.67.2: Having assumed this huge form that terrifies the world, O Rāma, I frighten the sages who have gone to the forest, here and there.
t.3.67.3: Then a great sage named Sthūlaśiras was angered by me; while he was gathering various forest produce, he was assaulted by me in this form.
t.3.67.4: Seeing me thus, he, pronouncer of a dreadful curse, said to me: "Let this very cruel and despised form be yours."
t.3.67.6: When Rāma, having cut off your two arms, burns you in the desolate forest, then you will regain your own form, vast and beautiful.
t.3.67.5: I entreated him in his anger, saying, 'May there be an end to this curse brought about by your imprecation,' and these words were spoken by him.
t.3.67.7: Know me, O Lakṣmaṇa, to be the son of Danu, once resplendent with glory; this form was thus obtained on the field of battle through the wrath of Indra.
t.3.67.8: For I pleased the Grandsire with fierce austerity, and he granted me a long life; thereupon delusion took hold of me.
t.3.67.9: "A long life has been obtained by me; what can Śakra do to me?" Resolving thus in my mind, I assailed Śakra in battle.
t.3.67.10: By the hundred-jointed thunderbolt hurled from his arm, both the thighs and the head were driven down into the body.
t.3.67.12: Struck down by the thunderbolt, with thighs, head and face shattered, and without food, how was I able to live on for so very long a time?
t.3.67.11: Though he was being entreated by me, he led me to the abode of Yama, and he said to me, "Let that word of the Grandfather be true."
t.3.67.13: Thus addressed by me, Śakra gave me two arms stretching a yojana in length, and fashioned in my belly a mouth with sharp fangs.
t.3.67.14: Such as I am, with my two long arms I drag in from every side the forest-roaming creatures, lions, elephants, deer and tigers, and devour them.
t.3.67.15: But Indra said to me: "When Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, cuts off your two arms in battle, then you will go to heaven."
t.3.67.16: You are that Rāma, may good fortune be yours! O Rāghava, I cannot be slain by anyone else; so the great sage truly declared.
t.3.67.18: Thus addressed by that Danu, the righteous-souled Rāghava spoke these words while Lakṣmaṇa listened.
t.3.67.17: For, O bull among men, once I have been purified by fire, I shall lend you the help of my counsel, and I shall point out a friend to you both.
t.3.67.19: My illustrious wife Sītā was carried off by Rāvaṇa when I had gone out from Janasthāna with my brother, as I pleased.
t.3.67.20: I know only the name of that rākṣasa, not his form; neither his dwelling nor his power do we know.
t.3.67.21: Toward those who are stricken with grief and without a protector, running about in this way, it is fitting to show compassion; so let your honor be engaged in helping us.
t.3.67.22: Having brought dry pieces of wood, broken off in time by elephants, we shall attend to you, O hero, in a great pit that has been prepared.
t.3.67.23: So tell me of Sītā, by whom she was carried off or to where. Do me this very great kindness, if you truly know.
t.3.67.24: Thus addressed by Rāma, Danu, skilled in speech, spoke these excellent words to Rāghava, who was himself an eloquent speaker.
t.3.67.25: I have no divine knowledge, and I do not know Maithilī. Once I am burned and have regained my own form, I shall tell you of one who will know of her.
t.3.67.26: For as long as I remain unburnt, O lord, I have no power to know that rākṣasa of great might by whom your Sītā was carried off.
t.3.67.27: My great knowledge has indeed been lost, O Rāghava, through the evil of a curse brought on by my own doing, and I have obtained a form reviled by the world.
t.3.67.28: But before the sun, whose horses are weary, goes down to its setting, cast me into a pit, O Rāma, and burn me according to the prescribed rite.
t.3.67.29: Once I have been burned by you in a pit in the proper manner, O Raghunandana, I shall tell you, O hero, of the one who will know that rākṣasa.
t.3.67.30: And friendship should be made with him, who is of righteous conduct, O Rāghava; pleased, that one of swift valour will render you assistance.
t.3.67.31: There is nothing in the three worlds unknown to him, O Rāghava, for long ago, for a certain reason, he wandered through all the worlds.
